name: Erich Honecker
role: German communist politician, General Secretary of the SED and head of state of the German Democratic Republic (1912-1994)
summary: Honecker's memoir and court statements defend public ownership of the means of production, the planned economy, agricultural cooperatives and the closed border of 1961, and blame Gorbachev's perestroika for the collapse of socialism in the GDR.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Article 35(3) of the 1974 constitution guaranteed that on the basis of a social insurance system, in illness and accidents, 'unentgeltliche ärztliche Hilfe, Arzneimittel und andere medizinische Sachleistungen' (free medical aid, medicines and other medical services) are granted to every citizen.

public-ownership.rationale: Article 12 of the GDR constitution, as revised in 1974 under his leadership, made mineral resources, mines, power plants, industrial enterprises, banks and insurance, transport and post 'Volkseigentum' (people's property) and declared 'Privateigentum daran ist unzulässig' (private ownership of them is inadmissible).

abortion-legal.rationale: The 9 March 1972 Law on the Interruption of Pregnancy, passed under his leadership, stated that the woman must be able to decide for herself on a pregnancy and its continuation, and allowed interruption on the woman's request by a doctor within 12 weeks, with a specialist commission deciding beyond that (§§ 1-2).

central-planning.rationale: Article 12(2) of the 1974 constitution names 'die sozialistische Planwirtschaft' (the socialist planned economy) as the means by which the state secures the highest result from people's property, and Article 24(3) makes socialist planning of the reproduction process a guarantee of the right to work.

one-party-rule.rationale: Article 1 of the GDR constitution as revised in 1974 defined the state as the political organisation of the working people 'unter Führung der Arbeiterklasse und ihrer marxistisch-leninistischen Partei' (under the leadership of the working class and its Marxist-Leninist party); the other parties sat in the National Front (Article 3) under that leadership.

collective-farming.rationale: In From My Life he presented the farmers' joining together in agricultural production cooperatives (LPG) in the 1950s as part of socialist progress, while private craftsmen and small entrepreneurs were also given a place; in 1993 he wrote that the aim of the 1989 counter-revolution was to 'liquidate the agricultural cooperatives' (my translation).

exit-over-voice.rationale: At the 45th session of the National Defence Council on 3 May 1974, which he chaired, he laid down that 'Grenzdurchbrüche überhaupt nicht zugelassen werden', that 'überall ein einwandfreies Schussfeld gewährleistet werden' must be assured and that 'nach wie vor muss bei Grenzdurchbruchsversuchen von der Schusswaffe rücksichtslos Gebrauch gemacht werden', with praise for those who used the firearm successfully.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Article 20(2) of the 1974 constitution states 'Mann und Frau sind gleichberechtigt und haben die gleiche Rechtsstellung in allen Bereichen des gesellschaftlichen, staatlichen und persönlichen Lebens' (men and women have equal rights and the same legal status in all areas), and Article 24(1) guarantees equal pay for equal work.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The 1968 constitution called the GDR 'ein sozialistischer Staat deutscher Nation' (Art. 1) and in Art. 8(2) committed it to seek 'die Überwindung der vom Imperialismus der deutschen Nation aufgezwungenen Spaltung' (overcoming the division imposed on the German nation by imperialism) and a step-by-step rapprochement towards unification; the revision of 7 October 1974, in his term as General Secretary, struck 'deutscher Nation' from Art. 1 and dropped the unification paragraph, leaving only the clause that the GDR will never wage a war of conquest (Art. 8).

notes: A first audit. Answers from his record as GDR leader (the constitution in force after the 1974 revision, the 1972 abortion law and the 3 May 1974 National Defence Council protocol) rest on those acts; the memoir and his 1992-93 statements (read by theme) support collective-farming and are otherwise not cited where an act answers. The sources are his 1981 memoir From My Life (read by theme: ownership, planning, agriculture, the border, the party and the churches), his 1992 court statement and his 1993 Moabit notes (both read in Spanish translation on the Marxists Internet Archive, by theme). Ten statements answered. The constitution's church article (Art. 39: churches order their affairs 'in accordance with the constitution and the laws') does not settle separate-church-state, which stays null; the 1972 speech on the world youth festival (Internet Archive) was read and states no position on a statement. The uncertainty rule is not met.
